events.title: Napoleon Escapes from Elba
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte slipped away from his exile on the island of Elba with about 1,000 men and sailed for France, landing near Antibes on March 1.
events.significance: His escape launched the Hundred Days, the final period of his rule, which ended with his defeat at Waterloo in June 1815 and his permanent exile to Saint Helena.

events.title: Birth of Levi Strauss
events.description: Levi Strauss, the Bavarian-born businessman, was born in Buttenheim. He later emigrated to the United States and settled in San Francisco.
events.significance: In 1873 he and Jacob Davis patented riveted work pants, creating blue jeans, which became one of the most enduring and influential garments in global fashion.

events.title: Grand Canyon National Park Established
events.description: President Woodrow Wilson signed legislation creating Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona, upgrading the site from national monument status.
events.significance: The act protected one of the world's most spectacular natural landscapes, which now draws millions of visitors each year and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

events.title: World Trade Center Bombing
events.description: A truck bomb exploded in the underground parking garage beneath the North Tower of the World Trade Center in New York City, killing six people and injuring more than 1,000.
events.significance: It was the first major foreign terrorist attack on the World Trade Center, prompting changes in US counterterrorism efforts and security, and foreshadowing the September 11, 2001 attacks.

events.title: Germany's Luftwaffe Officially Revealed
events.description: Adolf Hitler ordered the formal establishment of the Luftwaffe as a separate branch of the German military, openly violating the Treaty of Versailles.
events.significance: The open rearmament of German air power signaled Nazi Germany's defiance of postwar restrictions and was a key step toward the military buildup preceding World War II.
